svg.text: SOFTWARE 3
A cage in the flat branch of law 2: a ring of four seams, its swing and its persistence
the ring 0, 2, 4, 6 with the signs + − + −
At each port of the ring a plus meets a minus:
the port passes nothing on to its other seams.
Why the law keeps it

svg.text: Q adds the seams at a port without signs. The law moves e to e′
and back and to no other place: 4 seams and 28 wedges.
18 such profiles in a cell; its 30 rings span them.
On a federation: rings on ports with five seams.
+E = +2.4495 upper mode, empty in the reference
−E = −2.4495 lower mode, filled in the reference
lifting the object: a neutral excitation,
Kept exactly: [H, P_X] = 0 for the excitation, at every reading.
One added object in the upper mode costs E; the swing is at 2E.

svg.text: P_e = 1 − (σ²/E²) sin²(E t): a constant and one line at 2E
The pulse H − 2E n(e), for π / (2 √(2E(E − m))), puts the object of the
lower mode on e and does the work 3.456. Then no drive: the record
starts from rest and swings. The reference alone does not swing.
What observers read

Under a changed law
(seam hopping round every port, same
alphabet, routing and symmetry): no single
line, and 0.14 of the cage left at 64.
Supplied: the potential and the converter on e,
